---
title: "gtskill"
subtitle: "Can an AI agent write publication-quality data tables — reliably, cheaply, repeatably?"
---

`gtskill` is a small, testable evaluation harness that pairs the
[Claude Agent SDK](https://pypi.org/project/claude-agent-sdk/) with a
hand-tuned [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/)
*skill*, then measures — with a real evaluation loop — how much the
skill actually helps.

Give it a CSV and a natural-language prompt, and it produces a
formatted table plus a full audit trail: the `table.py` the agent
wrote, the rendered `table.png`, the transcript of the conversation,
tokens spent, cost, and a comparator score against ground truth.

## The headline result

We evaluated four different skill designs against a **no-skill
baseline** on the same 6-prompt corpus, at `--repeat 3` with the
auto-baseline. The winner:

| Skill | Accuracy (with skill) | Accuracy (no skill) | Lift | Cost / call |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **`prose`**   | **87.9%** | 15.8% | **+72.1** | \$0.16 |
| `scripts` | 87.7% | 19.0% | +68.7 | \$0.19 |
| `house`   | 83.5% | 20.1% | +63.4 | \$0.13 |
| `creator` | 21.7% | 24.9% | −3.2  | \$0.09 |

The prose skill takes a bare-LLM baseline from **16% to 88% accuracy**
— a **72-point lift** on the same prompts, same model, same data. For a
fraction of a cent per invocation.

![Accuracy: repeated with-skill samples vs. the unassisted baseline, across every corpus prompt.](assets/plots/prose/evaluation_score.png){fig-alt="Accuracy box plot for the prose skill on every corpus prompt, showing three runs per prompt and a baseline dot."}

The full per-skill, per-prompt breakdown — including individual runs
and per-prompt lift — is on the [Results](results.qmd) page.

## Who this is for

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### 📊 Data scientists

You have a dataset and want an AI-drafted table you can trust. Start
with [Setup](setup.qmd) → run your first `--skill prose` against your
own CSV → read the [Runner CLI](runner.qmd). The [prose skill](skills.qmd)
gets you 88% accuracy out of the box, and the rendered `table.png` is
publication-quality.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### 🧪 Skill authors

You want to build your own agent skill and measure it honestly. Read
[Methodology](methodology.qmd) for the loop, the comparator, the
judge, and the convergence report. Then read [Reproduce](reproduce.qmd)
to run it end-to-end against your own skill under
`.claude/skills/great-tables-creator/`.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### ⚙️ Harness builders

You want to see how a bounded, sandboxed, sidecar-Chrome-backed agent
runner is put together. Read [Harness](harness.qmd) for the
architecture, the per-run isolation, and the CDP rendering path.
Everything the runner does is one `run.py` invocation with one
[`RunSpec`](harness.qmd).
:::
:::

## What the harness produces

Every invocation writes one tree on disk:

```
runs/<type>/<timestamp>_<skill>_<slug>/
  run.json          # the RunSpec + resolved config + status + timings
  summary.json      # aggregate pass/fail + tokens/cost across prompts
  prompts/<name>/{baseline,repeat_1…N}/
    table.py         # the script the agent wrote
    table.png        # the rendered table
    transcript.json  # the SDK conversation
    data/ ...        # symlinked CSV — never copied
    .claude/ ...     # ephemeral, mounted skill root
  prompts/<name>/{convergence.json,contact_sheet.png}   # only when --repeat > 1
```

Nothing is hidden. The `transcript.json` is the writer's whole
conversation. The `report.txt` (when the prompt has ground truth) is
the check-by-check comparator scoring. See [Reproduce](reproduce.qmd)
for how to read it.

::: {.callout-tip}
